scan.summary: This is an inspection log for a Toyota propane-powered forklift (unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse, kept for September 2026 to satisfy OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), which requires daily examination of powered industrial trucks before use. The log tracks checklist items (tires, forks, mast, horn, lights, belt, brakes, steering, propane tank, fire extinguisher, data plate, overhead guard, and fuel level) completed on each shift, with operators signing off via initials and noting any defects. This is a working safety record maintained by the employer to document that the truck is safe before placing it in service each day.
scan.freshness_note: Log is current as of 17 September 2026. September 2026 inspections appear complete for working days so far; no future-dated entries. This is a monthly log sheet covering one month, so renewal (a new sheet for October) will be due when September ends.

gaps.title: Defect reporting and removal from service
gaps.description: Log shows one defect (Horn not working on Sep 9) but does not show that the truck was removed from service until repaired, or that the defect was reported to management immediately. OSHA 1910.178(q)(7) requires defects to be immediately reported and corrected, and the truck must not be placed in service if a condition adversely affects safety.
gaps.fix: Add a Notes column entry on Sep 9 stating when the horn was fixed, or add a separate defect log that shows the truck taken out of service, who was notified, and when the repair was completed. Require operators to mark defects and require supervisor sign-off that the truck was removed from service until repaired.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): 'Defects when found shall be immediately reported and corrected.'

gaps.title: Missing training documentation for inspectors
gaps.description: The log does not show that the operators performing inspections have been trained to conduct inspections properly. OSHA 1910.178(l) requires employers to train operators on inspection and maintenance tasks they will perform.
gaps.fix: Maintain a separate record of operator training and certification for pre-shift inspection tasks, with names, dates of training, and evaluator name for each operator shown on this log (M.C. and J.R.).
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(l): employer must provide training on vehicle inspection and maintenance

gaps.title: No specification of corrective action deadlines for defects
gaps.description: When defects are noted (X marking), there is no timeline or documentation showing when the truck is repaired and returned to service. The rule requires defects to be 'immediately reported and corrected'.
gaps.fix: When a defect is marked, add a follow-up row or notation stating the date and time the defect was reported, to whom, and the date the truck was repaired and returned to service. Establish a policy that defective trucks are taken out of service immediately.

conditions.evidence_expected: Completed inspection log with date, shift, hours, operator initials, and checklist items marked OK or X, with defects noted; log must be retained for audit

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence that this is a pre-shift inspection log maintained for compliance with OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). The document is clear, current, and contains all the required elements of a checklist (date, operator, checklist items, notes). Confidence is lower on whether the defect follow-up process is adequate, because the document does not show what happened after the horn defect was noted on Sep 9—there is no indication the truck was taken out of service or when/if it was repaired. The log also does not show the full names of operators or evidence that they have been trained on how to conduct the inspection. Initials alone may not be sufficient for OSHA record-keeping if the agency needs to audit individual operator training. No web search is needed to verify the citation to 1910.178(q)(7), as that is the standard regulation and is not subject to change.
